# ADR-004/W16 operational readiness evidence

Recorded on 2026-09-09 for the live pre-client Athenaeum deployment at
`athenaeum.callerscompendium.com`. This record contains no sync IDs, bearer
credentials, derived storage keys, manifest content, or SMTP credentials.

## Deployment identity

- A new operator began with only the existing Apache host and completed the
  first-deployment runbook from package installation through a working service.
- Deployed repository revision:
  `9cac24dca794621578caddd8c1a99a5757897cfd`.
- Container image: `callers-compendium-athenaeum:0.1`, image ID
  `sha256:e201dadc5f96bb842b2427ee67822a1d943ac68d7ee89f61487c9d48d21e5eb7`.
- The container used host networking and exposed no Docker-published port.
  Athenaeum listened only on `127.0.0.1:33333`.
- Apache terminated TLS, returned HTTP 403 for plaintext `/v1/store`, returned
  Athenaeum HTTP 401 for unauthenticated HTTPS `/v1/store`, and supplied
  `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000`.
- PR #1220 merged the deployed proxy and smoke-harness corrections as
  `d3e1004797e7380e9062532722c926ccf4ebbafc`. Before review hardening,
  `1801ce6e9133986fe8fb5ccaabf615fea16e948c` matched both deployed files
  byte-for-byte.

## Proxy conformance

The live smoke run passed:

- plaintext `/v1` refusal without redirect or proxying;
- separate real-client rate-limit buckets through Apache;
- overwrite of attacker-supplied `X-Forwarded-For`;
- the remaining server-wide failure budget after the client-bucket probes;
- 60 successful store creations and refusal of the 61st;
- authenticated HTTPS create and lookup with HSTS;
- preservation of request compression;
- the inclusive 16 MiB decoded request boundary; and
- a compressed 16 MiB request reaching Athenaeum.

Evidence log:
`/root/athenaeum-evidence/smoke-20260909T044945Z.log`.
SHA-256:
`2e17bb95abba7979bd502223305c4248674c13bdf03699a0abb1a0487196a3ea`.

## Alert delivery

### Quota exhaustion

- Exercise log:
  `/root/athenaeum-evidence/quota-20260909T052607Z.log`.
- A disposable store accepted 250 unique 1 MiB blobs and refused blob 251 with
  HTTP 507.
- The running service emitted `quota_exhaustion` with source `request` and error
  type `StoreQuotaExceeded`.
- The alert service was active.
- Fastmail delivered `Athenaeum alert: quota_exhaustion` to
  `themis@callerscompendium.com`, resolved to the operator's primary mailbox, at
  `2026-09-09T05:26:29Z`. Its body matched the emitted alert.

### Sweep failure

- A disposable store was backdated by 31 days and its directory permissions
  were deliberately restricted before the hourly sweep.
- The sweep removed the expired store metadata, retained one durable deletion
  job, and emitted `sweep_failure` with source `deletion_retry` and error type
  `PathAccessException`.
- Fastmail delivered `Athenaeum alert: sweep_failure` to
  `themis@callerscompendium.com` at `2026-09-09T06:57:32Z`. Its body matched the
  emitted alert.

## Retention

- After permissions were restored, an ordinary unauthenticated request
  triggered the pending cleanup retry and returned HTTP 401.
- The disposable store then had zero store, manifest, blob-reference, and
  deletion-job rows. Its epoch directory was absent.
- A count-only scan of the four Athenaeum Apache logs and container stderr found
  zero matches in every file for authorization headers, generated sync-ID
  shapes, and the `default_program_band` test-content marker.
- Evidence log:
  `/root/athenaeum-evidence/retention-20260909T071149Z.log`.
- SHA-256:
  `1689e9492e298f8e2fc472c7184048b555fb4e9165ea4570ff62d7117c1d876b`.

## Break-glass authorization

- The approval reference was published and merged before access:
  [Break-glass access record](https://callerscompendium.com/guide/breakglass-access-record.html)
  (PR #1211).
- The exercise ran at `2026-09-09T06:26:48Z` against one disposable store and
  its `device-one` manifest.
- Store, blob, and manifest preparation each returned HTTP 201.
- Matching rows in the separate break-glass database increased from zero to
  exactly one.
- The ordinary store database contained no break-glass table.
- The recovered secure test artifact was 228 bytes with SHA-256
  `23b3cd29585d7de5c1faed274a28a6cd4ace2d6515b3491767fe673d2c726ada`.
- The disposable store was deleted with HTTP 204.
- Exercise log:
  `/root/athenaeum-evidence/breakglass-20260909T062648Z.log`.

## Lost-ID support

The real disposable sweep store's raw sync ID was lost when its originating SSH
shell ended. Only the server's one-way derived key remained. The documented
support decision was exercised without a lookup or break-glass read: the ID
could not be recovered, and the required response was to create a new store and
configure a new sync ID.

## Deployment order

Existing beta releases contain Device Sync foundations but no user-facing
compatible client. At evidence time, W13's off-by-default settings and pairing
surface had no owning PR and remained incomplete, W14's review surface remained
incomplete, and the app exposed no Device Sync settings surface. Athenaeum was
therefore deployed and exercised before any compatible beta or public client
distribution.
